name: MathlibAnnex.aeConstantOn_of_countableCover
title: Gluing one almost-everywhere constant over a countable cover

content.display_title: Gluing one almost-everywhere constant over a countable cover
content.one_sentence_role: Combines local exceptional sets using an inequality between restricted measures.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $(X,\mu)$ be a measure space, $Y$ any set of values, $u:X\to Y$, and $c\in Y$. Let $U\subseteq X$, let $(V_i)_{i\in I}$ be any family of subsets, and let $T\subseteq I$ be countable. Suppose
$$U\subseteq\bigcup_{i\in T}V_i,\qquad
u=c\quad\mu|_{V_i}\text{-almost everywhere for every }i\in T.$$
Then $u=c$ almost everywhere for $\mu|_U$.
content.assumptions: There is no topology on $X$ or $Y$ in this statement. The function $u$, the cover members $V_i$, and $U$ need not be measurable. Only $T$ is countable; the index set $I$ need not be. All members use the same constant $c$.
content.conclusion: The one exceptional set $\{x:u(x)\ne c\}$ has measure zero for $\mu|_U$. The result includes the empty cover: the covering hypothesis then forces $U=\varnothing$.
content.proof_summary: Compare $\mu|_U$ with the sum of the restricted measures of the countable cover, and evaluate this inequality on the exceptional set.

proof_steps.text:
**Form a countable family of measures.** Reindex by $i\in T$ itself and write $B=\{x\in X:u(x)\ne c\}$. Restriction is monotone in its restricting set, and restriction to a countable union is bounded by the sum of the restrictions. Thus
$$\mu|_U\ \leq\ \mu|_{\bigcup_{i\in T}V_i}\ \leq\ \sum_{i\in T}\mu|_{V_i}.$$
These are measure inequalities; the restriction-to-union inequality does not require measurable cover members.

**Evaluate on the exceptional set.** Almost-everywhere equality on $V_i$ says $(\mu|_{V_i})(B)=0$. Evaluation of a countable sum of measures on any set therefore gives
$$0\leq(\mu|_U)(B)
\leq\left(\sum_{i\in T}\mu|_{V_i}\right)(B)
=\sum_{i\in T}(\mu|_{V_i})(B)=0.$$
Hence $(\mu|_U)(B)=0$, which is exactly the required almost-everywhere equality. No uncountable union of null sets enters this argument.

content.lean_realization_notes: The notation $\mu|_V$ means restriction of a measure to a set in the library's sense, which is defined even for a nonmeasurable $V$. The proof uses inequalities of measures and does not replace every restricted evaluation by an intersection formula requiring measurability.
